statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail risk sits in the watch band below the block threshold while Stress is high.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the mapped state is WATCH. The 17:00Z-20:00Z window covering the 30-year auction, Fed Musalem remarks and the US cash close is flagged as the narrow danger window. Existing-position management and protective logic are unaffected by this state.
headline: Oil above $100 and multidecade-high yields keep Stress high while an orderly two-sided Nasdaq-100 tape holds Tail in the watch band
body: The Nasdaq-100 trades at 30,998.74, down 0.52%, inside a two-sided intraday range of 30,918.77 to 31,125.13 after opening at 30,985.23 against a 31,160.08 previous close. The index bounced off the session low and sits mid-range rather than at an extreme, and VIX at 15.46 remains historically low. The macro backdrop is materially more hostile than the equity tape: Brent trades near $105 and WTI near $92.44, up roughly 4.7%, after a reported increase in Iranian attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and precautionary US Gulf production shut-ins ahead of a storm. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.28% with an intraday range of 5.27% to 5.33%, and the 30-year is near 5.67%, both close to multidecade highs amid a global bond selloff. The Federal Reserve raised rates at its September meeting on persistent inflation, and reporting indicates traders have added to bets on a further hike this year. Initial jobless claims for the week ended 3 October printed 197,000 against a 200,000 consensus, with continuing claims at 1.71 million, keeping the labour-market input firm. Internals are split: semiconductors lag clearly, with Arm down 4.3%, Intel down 3.1%, AMD down 1.9%, Micron down 1.4% and Nvidia down 0.8%, while Apple is up 0.5% and Netflix up 2.0% and the other megacaps are only marginally lower. The combination of an energy supply shock, long-end yields at multidecade highs and hawkish policy repricing is a genuinely difficult environment, which is reflected in high Stress. It has not, however, produced the pathological price path that Tail measures: the observed session shows a modest decline, two-way flow, a retracement off the low and subdued implied volatility rather than shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements or the index holding near a session extreme. Reported consideration of US military action against Iran is a credible discontinuity mechanism, but it is unobserved and conditional, so under this contract it informs Stress and Confidence rather than current Tail. Tail is therefore held at 22 in the watch band, with a narrow danger window across the 30-year auction, the Musalem remarks and the US cash close.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours began with a quiet, mean-reverting overnight tape in which Tail decayed from 18 to a low of 10 by 03:00Z while Stress drifted up from 52 to 50-53 on the building rates backdrop. From 06:00Z the oil and long-end-yield impulse became the dominant input: Tail stepped up to 22 at 07:00Z and held in a 20-23 watch-band range through the European and early US session, with Stress rising steadily from 55 to a 65-66 peak around 11:00Z-12:00Z. The 14:00Z slot briefly eased to Tail 17 as the US open proved orderly before the most recent hour returned to 20. Dominant mode was mixed throughout apart from three trend-down readings at 06:00Z, 07:00Z and 11:00Z. No hour in the window reached the block threshold, and no published hour is rewritten here.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail in the 21-23 watch band across the remaining US cash session, covering the 17:00Z 30-year auction, the 17:40Z Musalem remarks and the 20:00Z cash close, which together define the flagged danger window. Tail then decays into the low band through the post-close and Asian hours, reaching 14 between 02:00Z and 05:00Z, on the assumption that no fresh Hormuz or Iran policy headline arrives; such a headline is the stated invalidation. Risk rebuilds gradually across the European session from 15 at 06:00Z to 19 by 12:00Z, then returns to the watch band at 21-22 around the 13:30Z US cash open and the 14:00Z preliminary Michigan sentiment release, whose inflation-expectation components carry added weight with Brent above $100. Stress tracks the same shape at a higher level, easing from 68 to 52 overnight and rebuilding to 65, reflecting an unresolved oil-supply and rates backdrop rather than observed volatility expansion. All forward values are conditional risk, not an assertion that future price structure has been observed.
